source: arXiv API (export.arxiv.org); metadata verbatim, summaries hand-written from abstracts

topics.name: LULC classification with Sentinel-2 / Landsat and machine learning
topics.blurb: Core papers on supervised land use / land cover mapping from optical satellite imagery.

papers.title: Remote Sensing and Machine Learning-Based Analysis of Land Use and Vegetation Change in Dhaka District, Bangladesh
papers.summary: Uses Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 with NDVI, NDBI and NDWI in Google Earth Engine to track land use and vegetation change in Dhaka (2019-2024), comparing Decision Tree, KNN and Random Forest. Random Forest performed best, and the study documents rapid built-up expansion at the expense of vegetation and water.

papers.title: Continental-scale land cover mapping at 10 m resolution over Europe (ELC10)
papers.summary: Builds a 10 m land cover map of Europe (ELC10) with a Random Forest trained on LUCAS survey points inside Google Earth Engine. It reports that combining Sentinel-1 radar with Sentinel-2 optical data improved accuracy, while atmospheric correction and speckle filtering added little.

papers.title: Improvement in Land Cover and Crop Classification based on Temporal Features Learning from Sentinel-2 Data Using Recurrent-Convolutional Neural Network (R-CNN)
papers.summary: Proposes a recurrent-convolutional neural network that learns temporal features from multi-temporal Sentinel-2 imagery for pixel-based land cover and crop classification in northern Italy. It compares the deep model with traditional learners such as SVM and Random Forest.

papers.title: Deep learning in remote sensing: a review
papers.summary: A widely cited review of deep learning for remote sensing that discusses its challenges, recent advances and practical resources. Useful context for when tree ensembles are (and are not) the right tool.

topics.name: Ensemble learners and gradient boosting
topics.blurb: The algorithms behind XGBoost and CatBoost, and a recent benchmark of tree ensembles for urban land cover.

papers.title: Tabular Deep Learning vs Classical Machine Learning for Urban Land Cover Classification
papers.summary: Benchmarks classical models (including Random Forest, XGBoost and CatBoost) against tabular deep learning models on the UCI Urban Land Cover dataset, using macro-F1 and confusion matrices. Tree ensembles remain strong baselines, while tabular deep models can match them when imbalance is handled well.

papers.title: CatBoost: unbiased boosting with categorical features
papers.summary: Describes CatBoost's two key ideas, ordered boosting and a new way of handling categorical features, both designed to stop the 'prediction shift' caused by target leakage in standard gradient boosting.

papers.title: XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System
papers.summary: The original XGBoost paper: a scalable tree-boosting system with a sparsity-aware split algorithm and weighted quantile sketch. It explains why XGBoost became a default strong baseline for tabular data.

topics.name: Explainable AI and SHAP
topics.blurb: Shapley-value explanations, tree-specific SHAP, and explainability reviews for remote sensing.

papers.title: Opening the Black-Box: A Systematic Review on Explainable AI in Remote Sensing
papers.journal_ref: published in IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Magazine, vol. 12, no. 4, pp. 261-304, Dec. 2024
papers.summary: A systematic review of explainable AI in remote sensing: which methods are used, what they are used for, how explanations are interpreted and evaluated, and open challenges. A good map of the field for newcomers.

papers.title: ML4EJ: Decoding the Role of Urban Features in Shaping Environmental Injustice Using Interpretable Machine Learning
papers.summary: Uses Random Forest and XGBoost with feature-importance analysis to study how urban features, including land cover and infrastructure, shape exposure to air pollution, heat and flooding across six US counties. An example of interpretable ML applied to urban geography.

papers.title: Towards Explainable Land Cover Mapping: a Counterfactual-based Strategy
papers.summary: Proposes a GAN-based counterfactual explanation method for land cover classification from satellite image time series, showing what minimal, time-localised changes would flip a prediction to another class.

papers.title: Explainable AI for Trees: From Local Explanations to Global Understanding
papers.summary: Presents TreeSHAP, a polynomial-time algorithm for exact Shapley-value explanations of tree models, plus interaction values and tools for turning many local explanations into global understanding. Directly relevant to explaining Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM and CatBoost.

papers.title: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions
papers.summary: Introduces SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), a unified framework that assigns each feature an importance value for a single prediction, grounded in game-theoretic Shapley values. This is the method behind most SHAP plots in LULC papers.

topics.name: Spectral indices, multi-source data and fusion
topics.blurb: Combining optical bands, radar, indices (NDVI, NDBI, ...) and auxiliary geographic layers.

papers.title: Causal Evaluation of Contributing Factors to Urban Heat Island
papers.summary: Analyses urban heat island drivers across Tehran's districts (2003-2021) using NDVI, EVI, NDBI, NDWI and NDSI time series with a Hotelling's T-square based causal test. Useful for seeing how spectral indices are interpreted as urban and vegetation proxies.

papers.title: Using Multiple Input Modalities Can Improve Data-Efficiency and O.O.D. Generalization for ML with Satellite Imagery
papers.summary: Shows that appending extra geographic layers (e.g. elevation and other non-optical inputs) to satellite imagery improves ML performance, especially with little labelled data and in out-of-region tests. Simple hard-coded fusion often beat learned fusion.

papers.title: Land use/land cover classification of fused Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imageries using ensembles of Random Forests
papers.summary: Fuses Sentinel-1 SAR texture with Sentinel-2 VNIR-SWIR bands (Bayesian fusion) and classifies LULC with ensembles of Random Forests built with random rotations. It evaluates how fusion and rotation strategy affect accuracy.

topics.name: Sampling, validation and spatial pitfalls
topics.blurb: Reference data quality, spatial cross-validation and over-optimistic accuracy.

papers.title: A Bayesian Inference Approach for Reducing Inter-Investigator Variability in Sampling-Based Land Cover Classification
papers.summary: Studies how different people labelling reference samples changes land cover results (44 investigators, Saitama, Japan) and proposes a Bayesian (Dirichlet) fusion of classification maps to reduce that variability and salt-and-pepper noise.

papers.title: Importance of spatial predictor variable selection in machine learning applications -- Moving from data reproduction to spatial prediction
papers.summary: Demonstrates with Random Forest land cover and LAI case studies that random cross-validation gives over-optimistic accuracy for spatial data, and that spatial cross-validation plus spatial variable selection are needed. Location-like predictors can cause severe overfitting.

topics.name: Africa, Nigeria and fast-growing cities
topics.blurb: Land cover and settlement mapping in African and other rapidly urbanising contexts.

papers.title: A High Resolution Urban and Rural Settlement Map of Africa Using Deep Learning and Satellite Imagery
papers.summary: Produces a 10 m urban-rural settlement map for Africa (2016-2022) with a DeepLabV3 model fusing Landsat-8, VIIRS night lights, ESRI LULC and GHS-SMOD, validated against DHS survey labels.

papers.title: Evaluating the Role of Training Data Origin for Country-Scale Cropland Mapping in Data-Scarce Regions: A Case Study of Nigeria
papers.journal_ref: ISPRS Open J. Photogramm. Remote Sens. 17 (2025) 100091
papers.summary: Country-scale cropland mapping in Nigeria with Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, ERA5 climate and a DEM in Google Earth Engine, comparing Random Forest and LSTMs. Local (Nigeria-only) training data beat larger global datasets, and radar, climate and topography were important inputs.

papers.title: How accurate are existing land cover maps for agriculture in Sub-Saharan Africa?
papers.summary: Compares 11 public land cover maps against rigorous reference data from 8 Sub-Saharan African countries to see which identify cropland best. A reminder that global products can disagree strongly in African landscapes.

papers.title: Quality Assessment of the 20m SPOT DEM in Nigeria
papers.summary: Assesses the vertical accuracy of the 20 m SPOT DEM against 780 ground control points in Lagos State and the FCT (Abuja), across land cover types. Relevant when using elevation, slope and aspect as features for Abuja-area studies.

topics.name: Benchmark datasets
topics.blurb: Large labelled Sentinel datasets for training and comparing LULC models.

papers.title: BigEarthNet: A Large-Scale Benchmark Archive For Remote Sensing Image Understanding
papers.summary: Introduces BigEarthNet, a large multi-label archive of 590,326 Sentinel-2 patches labelled from CORINE Land Cover 2018. Shows that models trained on it outperform ImageNet-pretrained CNNs for RS scene classification.

papers.title: SEN12MS -- A Curated Dataset of Georeferenced Multi-Spectral Sentinel-1/2 Imagery for Deep Learning and Data Fusion
papers.summary: SEN12MS: 180,662 georeferenced triplets of Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 multispectral patches and MODIS land cover covering all inhabited continents and seasons, built for deep learning and data fusion.

papers.title: EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification
papers.summary: Introduces EuroSAT: 27,000 labelled, geo-referenced Sentinel-2 patches across 10 LULC classes and all 13 bands, with CNN baselines. A standard starter dataset for LULC classification.
